description:
A dozen headline indicators — population, median household income, per capita income, the poverty rate, the unemployment rate, median age, the bachelor's-degree-or-higher share, the share of people of color, households, the owner-occupied share, median home value and median gross rent — carried across two non-overlapping ACS 5-year releases: **2015-2019** (`acsdt5y2019`, the Census Bureau's table-based [prototype summary file](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2019/prototype/5YRData/), validated against the [Census API](https://api.census.gov/data/2019/acs/acs5) before this collection was built — 29 requests, ~4.66 million compared values across every summary level this catalog uses including block groups, 0 mismatches) and **2020-2024** (`acsdt5y2024`, the same release every other ACS collection here reads). **Long form**: one row per `geoid` per `period`, not one row per geoid — a consumer who wants "both years side by side" pivots on `period`, and the `chg_*` columns already carry the 2020-2024-minus-2015-2019 difference on the 2020-2024 row so a map style can classify on it without a join.

All **112** rows at this geography (56 states and state equivalents × 2 periods), in the United States, Puerto Rico and the island areas.

**The two periods do not overlap, which is what makes them comparable.** 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 share no sample year, unlike two 5-year releases one year apart (2019-2023 and 2020-2024, say), which the Census Bureau's own guidance on [Comparing ACS Data](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/guidance/comparing-acs-data.html) says not to compare because their overlapping sample years make a measured difference partly an artifact of shared data. This collection's two periods are five years apart with no shared sample year, so a difference here is a measured change, not a sampling artifact of the comparison itself — though it is still a difference of two margin-of-error estimates, see `chg_*_moe` and the known issues before calling a small difference real.

**`geo_change` is measured per geoid, not assumed** — see the column's own description for the full definition of each value. At this geography: `identical` (92.9%, 52 of 56); `no_acs_data` (7.1%, 4). Never apportioned: the period a geoid's lineage does not support a legitimate figure for carries NULL on the affected columns rather than a modelled or carried-over number dressed up as a measurement.

Every estimate ships with its margin of error — `<column>_moe`, at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes — and the headline statistics also carry a coefficient of variation (`<column>_cv` = `moe / 1.645 / estimate`) so small-area noise can be flagged rather than mapped as if certain. Derived percentages propagate error with the Census Bureau's own formulas from [ACS Accuracy of the Data](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/tech_docs/accuracy/MultiyearACSAccuracyofData2024.pdf): sums add in quadrature, proportions use the subset formula with the ratio formula as fallback. ACS jam values for suppressed or unestimable cells are NULL here, never numbers, and medians are published as the Bureau publishes them — a median cannot be aggregated to a larger area. Each column's description names its ACS table, its exact universe, and the lines summed to make it.

Geometries are the Census Bureau's [2024 cartographic boundary files](https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/cartographic-boundary.html) for states and state equivalents (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), reprojected to EPSG:4326 and joined on `GEOID`. Cartographic rather than TIGER/Line because TIGER extends census geographies into open water while the cartographic files clip to the shoreline, which is what a choropleth wants. The boundary vintage matches the estimate vintage.

Three collections, one per geography: [Trends, 2015–2024 — Counties](../county-trends/collection.json) and [Trends, 2015–2024 — Census Tracts](../tract-trends/collection.json). All three carry the same dozen indicators and the same `geo_change` taxonomy; they do not join to each other on `geoid` (a tract is not a county). This group sits beside the ACS themed chunks at the same geographies, not inside them — a different shape (long form, two periods, `geo_change`) from every themed collection this catalog otherwise publishes, and it carries only 12 of the catalog's ~135 indicators rather than a theme's full set. For every other 2020-2024 indicator at this geography, or for a 2020-2024-only question with no time dimension, see [states](../../states/catalog.json).

The PMTiles archive carries the same columns as the GeoParquet minus the `*_moe` columns, at every zoom, for the `2020-2024` period's features only (one geometry per geoid, with its `chg_*` columns already on it — tiling both periods' identical geometries twice would double the archive for no visual gain). Built with [tylertoo](https://github.com/geoparquet-io/tylertoo). Statistics come from the GeoParquet, which keeps both periods.

This is a mirror — [data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/) is authoritative, and nothing here is an official Census Bureau product. The exact upstream files this collection was built from are published as `source` assets, linked at their original census.gov URLs, so the original is always one click away; the Bureau's own documentation is linked alongside them. Read the collection's [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) before querying: it carries the schema, the join keys, the NULL-rate story and tested queries against the published URLs.

table:columns.name: geoid
table:columns.description: 2-character state FIPS code, e.g. `29` for Missouri. Covers the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and the four island areas. Matches `GEOID` in the 2024 cartographic boundary state file; the ACS `0400000US` prefix is stripped. Keyed to the geography the 2020-2024 ACS release tabulates (the same geoid every other collection at this geography uses); a 2015-2019 predecessor that no longer exists under this geoid (Connecticut's 8 old counties, Alaska's Valdez-Cordova Census Area) is not published as a row of its own -- see `geo_change`.

table:columns.name: name
table:columns.description: State name from the cartographic boundary state file's `NAME` field — "Missouri".

table:columns.name: state
table:columns.description: Two-letter USPS state or territory code (`MO`, `PR`, `GU`). Carried on every collection from the `STATEFP → USPS` lookup embedded in `tools/specs.py` rather than read off the boundary files, because the 2024 cartographic boundary block-group file has no `STUSPS` column while the tract, county and state files do.

table:columns.name: period
table:columns.description: Which ACS 5-year release this row's estimates come from: `2015-2019` (`acsdt5y2019`, the Census Bureau's table-based prototype summary file, validated against the Census API with 0 mismatches across ~4.66 million compared values before this collection was built) or `2020-2024` (`acsdt5y2024`, the same release every other ACS collection in this catalog reads). The two periods do not overlap, which is what makes them comparable in the first place -- see the collection's known_issues and [Comparing ACS Data](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/guidance/comparing-acs-data.html).

table:columns.name: geo_change
table:columns.description:
How this row's geoid relates across the two periods -- measured against the real geometry change between the 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 vintages (population-weighted at tract level, via catalog/reference/crosswalks/t10t20-tract.parquet and catalog/blocks' 2020 population; exact at county level, via the preserved 6-digit tract number for Connecticut's 2022 county realignment), never assumed. One of five values:

- `identical` -- bidirectionally 1:1: this geoid's predecessor sent essentially all (>=99%) of its population here, and this geoid received essentially all of its population from that one predecessor. All 12 indicators carry over.
- `absorbed` -- several clean predecessors (each sending >=99% of ITS OWN population here) combine into this geoid. Counts (`population`, `households`) SUM across the predecessors' raw census cells with margins added in quadrature -- a legitimate aggregation -- and the five rate columns (`pct_below_poverty`, `pct_unemployed`, `pct_bachelors_plus`, `pct_people_of_color`, `pct_owner_occupied`) recompute from the summed numerator and denominator. The five medians (`median_hh_income`, `per_capita_income`, `median_age`, `median_home_value`, `median_gross_rent`) are NULL for the 2015-2019 period: a median cannot be derived from medians, so there is no legitimate figure for a geography the Census Bureau never tabulated directly.
- `subdivided` -- this geoid gets >=99% of its population from a single predecessor, but that predecessor itself sends population to more than one place (it is not a clean 1:1 match on its own side). The five rates and five medians carry over from that one predecessor under an explicit part-resembles-whole assumption -- flagged here, not hidden -- while `population` and `households` are NULL: carrying a whole predecessor's population onto a fragment of it would overstate the fragment.
- `mixed` -- genuinely mixed sources: no predecessor dominates and no clean set of feeders combines cleanly either. Every indicator is NULL for the 2015-2019 period.
- `no_acs_data` -- a cartographic boundary exists and the ACS 5-year program tabulates NEITHER period here (American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, the U.S. Virgin Islands). Not a geography change -- a program gap in both periods.

The period with no legitimate figure carries NULL, never an apportioned or carried-over number dressed up as a measurement. See the collection's known_issues for the measured share of each category and the Connecticut/Alaska specifics.

table:columns.name: population
table:columns.description: Total population. Universe: total population. The single line of [B01003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01003) (Total Population), published as an integer. Carried on every ACS collection so a rate can be weighted or sanity-checked without a second download. Carried for both the 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 periods (see `period`); NULL for whichever period `geo_change` says has no legitimate figure, never an apportioned or carried-over number.

table:columns.name: population_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `population` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: chg_population
table:columns.description: `population` in the `2020-2024` row minus `population` in the `2015-2019` row for the same `geoid`, carried on the `2020-2024` row only -- change belongs to the endpoint, not to either period alone, and a map style cannot compute a difference across two rows at render time. NULL on every `2015-2019` row, and NULL on a `2020-2024` row wherever either period's `population` is NULL -- which already encodes `geo_change` correctly: a `subdivided` geoid has no `chg_population`/`chg_households` but does have the rate and median `chg_*` columns, and `absorbed` is the mirror image. `chg_pct_below_poverty` is the column the collection's diverging style classifies on, not this one.

table:columns.name: chg_population_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `chg_population`: `sqrt(moe_2020_2024² + moe_2015_2019²)`, the Census Bureau's quadrature formula for the margin of a difference between two independent estimates (ACS Accuracy of the Data). NULL wherever `chg_population` is NULL.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income
table:columns.description: Median household income in the past 12 months, in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars. Universe: households. Line 1 of [B19013](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013), published as the Census Bureau publishes it. A median cannot be aggregated: there is no way to combine the medians of two block groups into the median of their union. Carried for both the 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 periods (see `period`); NULL for whichever period `geo_change` says has no legitimate figure, never an apportioned or carried-over number.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `median_hh_income` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: chg_median_hh_income
table:columns.description: `median_hh_income` in the `2020-2024` row minus `median_hh_income` in the `2015-2019` row for the same `geoid`, carried on the `2020-2024` row only -- change belongs to the endpoint, not to either period alone, and a map style cannot compute a difference across two rows at render time. NULL on every `2015-2019` row, and NULL on a `2020-2024` row wherever either period's `median_hh_income` is NULL -- which already encodes `geo_change` correctly: a `subdivided` geoid has no `chg_population`/`chg_households` but does have the rate and median `chg_*` columns, and `absorbed` is the mirror image. **Not on a common dollar basis**: each ACS release reports this column in its OWN vintage's inflation-adjusted dollars, not re-based to a common dollar-year here, so this difference mixes real change with five years of inflation -- measured at state level, 52 of 52 states show a nominal increase and 0 a decrease, which is this build's own evidence that the comparison is partly a dollar-basis effect. Deflate to a common dollar-year (e.g. CPI-U-RS) before treating this as a real-dollar change.

table:columns.name: chg_median_hh_income_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `chg_median_hh_income`: `sqrt(moe_2020_2024² + moe_2015_2019²)`, the Census Bureau's quadrature formula for the margin of a difference between two independent estimates (ACS Accuracy of the Data). NULL wherever `chg_median_hh_income` is NULL.

table:columns.name: per_capita_income
table:columns.description: Per capita income in the past 12 months, in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars — aggregate income divided by total population, so children and people with no income are in the denominator. Universe: total population. Line 1 of [B19301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19301). Carried for both the 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 periods (see `period`); NULL for whichever period `geo_change` says has no legitimate figure, never an apportioned or carried-over number.

table:columns.name: per_capita_income_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `per_capita_income` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: chg_per_capita_income
table:columns.description: `per_capita_income` in the `2020-2024` row minus `per_capita_income` in the `2015-2019` row for the same `geoid`, carried on the `2020-2024` row only -- change belongs to the endpoint, not to either period alone, and a map style cannot compute a difference across two rows at render time. NULL on every `2015-2019` row, and NULL on a `2020-2024` row wherever either period's `per_capita_income` is NULL -- which already encodes `geo_change` correctly: a `subdivided` geoid has no `chg_population`/`chg_households` but does have the rate and median `chg_*` columns, and `absorbed` is the mirror image. **Not on a common dollar basis**: each ACS release reports this column in its OWN vintage's inflation-adjusted dollars, not re-based to a common dollar-year here, so this difference mixes real change with five years of inflation -- measured at state level, 52 of 52 states show a nominal increase and 0 a decrease, which is this build's own evidence that the comparison is partly a dollar-basis effect. Deflate to a common dollar-year (e.g. CPI-U-RS) before treating this as a real-dollar change.

table:columns.name: chg_per_capita_income_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `chg_per_capita_income`: `sqrt(moe_2020_2024² + moe_2015_2019²)`, the Census Bureau's quadrature formula for the margin of a difference between two independent estimates (ACS Accuracy of the Data). NULL wherever `chg_per_capita_income` is NULL.

table:columns.name: pct_below_poverty
table:columns.description: Percent of the population below the federal poverty level — an income-to-poverty ratio under 1.00. Universe: population for whom poverty status is determined, which excludes institutionalized people, people in military group quarters and in college dormitories, and unrelated individuals under 15. Lines 2 ("Under .50") + 3 (".50 to .99") of [C17002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.C17002) over line 1. Carried for both the 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 periods (see `period`); NULL for whichever period `geo_change` says has no legitimate figure, never an apportioned or carried-over number.

table:columns.name: pct_below_poverty_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_below_poverty` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: chg_pct_below_poverty
table:columns.description: `pct_below_poverty` in the `2020-2024` row minus `pct_below_poverty` in the `2015-2019` row for the same `geoid`, carried on the `2020-2024` row only -- change belongs to the endpoint, not to either period alone, and a map style cannot compute a difference across two rows at render time. NULL on every `2015-2019` row, and NULL on a `2020-2024` row wherever either period's `pct_below_poverty` is NULL -- which already encodes `geo_change` correctly: a `subdivided` geoid has no `chg_population`/`chg_households` but does have the rate and median `chg_*` columns, and `absorbed` is the mirror image. This is the column the collection's diverging style classifies on.

table:columns.name: chg_pct_below_poverty_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `chg_pct_below_poverty`: `sqrt(moe_2020_2024² + moe_2015_2019²)`, the Census Bureau's quadrature formula for the margin of a difference between two independent estimates (ACS Accuracy of the Data). NULL wherever `chg_pct_below_poverty` is NULL.

table:columns.name: pct_unemployed
table:columns.description: Unemployment rate: unemployed people as a percent of the civilian labor force. Universe for the table is the population 16 years and over, but the denominator here is line 3, "Civilian labor force" — the labor force, not the whole population 16+, because that is what an unemployment rate divides by. Line 5 ("Unemployed") over line 3 of [B23025](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B23025). Members of the Armed Forces and people not in the labor force are excluded from both parts. Carried for both the 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 periods (see `period`); NULL for whichever period `geo_change` says has no legitimate figure, never an apportioned or carried-over number.

table:columns.name: median_age
table:columns.description: Median age in years. Universe: total population. Line 1 of [B01002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01002) (Median Age by Sex); the male and female medians on lines 2 and 3 are not published here. Like every median, not aggregable. Carried for both the 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 periods (see `period`); NULL for whichever period `geo_change` says has no legitimate figure, never an apportioned or carried-over number.

table:columns.name: median_age_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `median_age` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: chg_median_age
table:columns.description: `median_age` in the `2020-2024` row minus `median_age` in the `2015-2019` row for the same `geoid`, carried on the `2020-2024` row only -- change belongs to the endpoint, not to either period alone, and a map style cannot compute a difference across two rows at render time. table:columns.name: pct_bachelors_plus

Lines 22–25 of [B15003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B15003) (Bachelor's, Master's, Professional school, Doctorate) over line 1. Associate's degrees (line 21) are deliberately excluded. Carried for both the 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 periods (see `period`); NULL for whichever period `geo_change` says has no legitimate figure, never an apportioned or carried-over number.

A complement, so it carries `pct_white_nh`'s own margin of error unchanged — a share and its complement have the same sampling error. Carried for both the 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 periods (see `period`); NULL for whichever period `geo_change` says has no legitimate figure, never an apportioned or carried-over number.

table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_people_of_color` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. A complement carries the margin of error of the share it was taken from, unchanged — `100 − p` has the same sampling error as `p`.

table:columns.name: households

Line 1 of [B25003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25003) (Tenure), published as an integer. Carried for both the 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 periods (see `period`); NULL for whichever period `geo_change` says has no legitimate figure, never an apportioned or carried-over number.

table:columns.description: Margin of error for `households` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: pct_owner_occupied
table:columns.description: Percent of occupied housing units that are owner-occupied. Universe: occupied housing units. Line 2 ("Owner occupied") over line 1 of [B25003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25003). The homeownership rate of households, not of people, and vacant units are outside the universe entirely. Carried for both the 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 periods (see `period`); NULL for whichever period `geo_change` says has no legitimate figure, never an apportioned or carried-over number.

table:columns.name: pct_owner_occupied_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_owner_occupied` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: chg_pct_owner_occupied
table:columns.description: `pct_owner_occupied` in the `2020-2024` row minus `pct_owner_occupied` in the `2015-2019` row for the same `geoid`, carried on the `2020-2024` row only -- change belongs to the endpoint, not to either period alone, and a map style cannot compute a difference across two rows at render time. NULL on every `2015-2019` row, and NULL on a `2020-2024` row wherever either period's `pct_owner_occupied` is NULL -- which already encodes `geo_change` correctly: a `subdivided` geoid has no `chg_population`/`chg_households` but does have the rate and median `chg_*` columns, and `absorbed` is the mirror image. `chg_pct_below_poverty` is the column the collection's diverging style classifies on, not this one.

table:columns.name: chg_pct_owner_occupied_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `chg_pct_owner_occupied`: `sqrt(moe_2020_2024² + moe_2015_2019²)`, the Census Bureau's quadrature formula for the margin of a difference between two independent estimates (ACS Accuracy of the Data). NULL wherever `chg_pct_owner_occupied` is NULL.

table:columns.name: median_home_value
table:columns.description: Median value of owner-occupied housing units, in dollars — the owner's estimate of what the property would sell for, not an assessment or a sale price. Universe: owner-occupied housing units. Line 1 of [B25077](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25077). Carried for both the 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 periods (see `period`); NULL for whichever period `geo_change` says has no legitimate figure, never an apportioned or carried-over number.

table:columns.name: median_home_value_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `median_home_value` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: chg_median_home_value
table:columns.description: `median_home_value` in the `2020-2024` row minus `median_home_value` in the `2015-2019` row for the same `geoid`, carried on the `2020-2024` row only -- change belongs to the endpoint, not to either period alone, and a map style cannot compute a difference across two rows at render time. NULL on every `2015-2019` row, and NULL on a `2020-2024` row wherever either period's `median_home_value` is NULL -- which already encodes `geo_change` correctly: a `subdivided` geoid has no `chg_population`/`chg_households` but does have the rate and median `chg_*` columns, and `absorbed` is the mirror image. **Not on a common dollar basis**: each ACS release reports this column in its OWN vintage's inflation-adjusted dollars, not re-based to a common dollar-year here, so this difference mixes real change with five years of inflation -- measured at state level, 52 of 52 states show a nominal increase and 0 a decrease, which is this build's own evidence that the comparison is partly a dollar-basis effect. Deflate to a common dollar-year (e.g. CPI-U-RS) before treating this as a real-dollar change.

table:columns.name: chg_median_home_value_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `chg_median_home_value`: `sqrt(moe_2020_2024² + moe_2015_2019²)`, the Census Bureau's quadrature formula for the margin of a difference between two independent estimates (ACS Accuracy of the Data). NULL wherever `chg_median_home_value` is NULL.

table:columns.name: median_gross_rent
table:columns.description: Median gross rent in dollars per month — contract rent plus the estimated average monthly cost of utilities and fuels. Universe: renter-occupied housing units **paying cash rent**, so units occupied rent-free are excluded. Line 1 of [B25064](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25064). Carried for both the 2015-2019 and 2020-2024 periods (see `period`); NULL for whichever period `geo_change` says has no legitimate figure, never an apportioned or carried-over number.

table:columns.name: median_gross_rent_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `median_gross_rent` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: chg_median_gross_rent
table:columns.description: `median_gross_rent` in the `2020-2024` row minus `median_gross_rent` in the `2015-2019` row for the same `geoid`, carried on the `2020-2024` row only -- change belongs to the endpoint, not to either period alone, and a map style cannot compute a difference across two rows at render time. NULL on every `2015-2019` row, and NULL on a `2020-2024` row wherever either period's `median_gross_rent` is NULL -- which already encodes `geo_change` correctly: a `subdivided` geoid has no `chg_population`/`chg_households` but does have the rate and median `chg_*` columns, and `absorbed` is the mirror image. **Not on a common dollar basis**: each ACS release reports this column in its OWN vintage's inflation-adjusted dollars, not re-based to a common dollar-year here, so this difference mixes real change with five years of inflation -- measured at state level, 52 of 52 states show a nominal increase and 0 a decrease, which is this build's own evidence that the comparison is partly a dollar-basis effect. Deflate to a common dollar-year (e.g. CPI-U-RS) before treating this as a real-dollar change.

table:columns.name: chg_median_gross_rent_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `chg_median_gross_rent`: `sqrt(moe_2020_2024² + moe_2015_2019²)`, the Census Bureau's quadrature formula for the margin of a difference between two independent estimates (ACS Accuracy of the Data). NULL wherever `chg_median_gross_rent` is NULL.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Boundary polygon (Polygon or MultiPolygon), WKB-encoded, in EPSG:4326 / OGC:CRS84 — the GeoParquet default CRS, written as an omitted `crs` key. From the Census Bureau's 2024 cartographic boundary state file (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), which clips to the shoreline — TIGER/Line would extend the state into open water. Generalized for mapping and point-in-polygon work, not for legal-boundary or precise-area work.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.type: struct<xmin: double, ymin: double, xmax: double, ymax: double>
table:columns.description: GeoParquet 1.1 covering struct (`xmin`, `ymin`, `xmax`, `ymax`) for the row's geometry, with row-group statistics, so a spatial filter can skip most of the file over the network. Written by geoparquet-io, not by the Census Bureau.

doc-comparing-acs.title: Comparing ACS Data — Census Bureau guidance
doc-comparing-acs.description: The Census Bureau's own guidance on which ACS period pairs can be compared: non-overlapping 5-year periods (this collection's 2015-2019 and 2020-2024) can be; overlapping ones cannot, because shared sample years make a measured difference partly an artifact of the comparison itself.

doc-acs-accuracy.title: ACS Accuracy of the Data (2024, multiyear estimates)
doc-acs-accuracy.description: The source of the quadrature formula `chg_*_moe` applies to the difference of two periods' margins, and of every other margin-of-error formula this build applies.
